name: AI Agent Kill Switch
description: Stop a compromised or runaway AI agent. Ordered least-destructive first: block its key at the gateway (reversible), kill the process on its device, then — only after a human has approved — revoke the provider key and the application's OAuth grant, neither of which can be undone. Every step is graded on its own capability contract at dispatch; approving this playbook does not authorise what its steps contain.
author: AiSOC maintainers

agent_id.description: The agent to stop, as the AI estate inventory records it

gateway_key.description: Virtual key the agent calls through, if it routes via a gateway

device.description: Device the agent process runs on, from the inventory's HOSTS edge

key_id.description: Model-provider key id. Not the secret: the secret never reaches AiSOC

client_id.description: OAuth client id of the AI application, where one is involved

steps.name: Pull the agent's inventory record: person, device, permissions
Block the agent's key at the gateway (reversible)
Kill the agent process on its device
Tell the SOC channel what has been contained so far

params.message_template: AI kill switch engaged for agent {{inputs.agent_id}}. Gateway key blocked and process killed. Awaiting approval for the irreversible half.

params.prompt: Revoke the provider key and the application's OAuth grant? Neither can be undone by AiSOC: a revoked key has no un-delete, and a re-granted OAuth consent is the user consenting again in their own browser. Everything reversible has already been done.

steps.name: Revoke the AI application's OAuth grant (irreversible)
Record what was contained, and what was not

params.title: AI agent kill switch: {{inputs.agent_id}}
params.description: Gateway key blocked, process killed, provider key and OAuth grant revoked where present. A step whose condition was false did not run and nothing here should be read as it having succeeded.
